clue.text: Switch positions from time to time

definitions.meaning: the two settings a light switch can be put in

explanation.surface: Someone changes jobs or places every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch has two settings, and something done intermittently happens in fits and starts, so both senses fit the phrase.

clue.text: Lots of food? Not for starters

indicators.note: Not for starters says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: noodles are a food, strips of pasta

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether there's much to eat but skips the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a great quantity, a synonym of lots.

clue.text: A breather after climbing a high rocky hill to find reptile

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A hiker takes a rest after scaling a craggy peak and meets a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns GILL upwards to LLIG; 'breather' looks like a rest but is the fish's organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The large-jawed American crocodilian is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Several English, assorted

parts.note: divers is an archaic word for several or sundry

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of English items.
explanation.definitionFit: Varied and of many kinds is a synonym of assorted.

clue.text: Conflict involving old offensive

indicators.note: involving says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a fray is a fight or conflict

explanation.surface: A war that included a bygone attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive as a noun means an attack, and a raid into enemy territory is one.

clue.text: Bright cold bar

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A chilly but well-lit pub or a cheerful cold drinking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of intelligent is a synonym for quick-witted and smart.

clue.text: Serving US soldier in one's pub is only to be expected

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: your local is your nearest or regular pub
GI is the standard term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A serving American soldier at the neighbourhood pub is no surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural, reasonable outcome follows sensibly, which is what this adjective conveys.

clue.text: One's played Shakespearean heroine

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument, something a musician plays
the heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as Cesario

explanation.surface: An actress has taken the role of a Shakespeare leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a stringed instrument slightly larger than the violin and the twin in Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Herb garden enthralling the old lady

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a rosery is a rose garden
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A garden that captivates someone's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic needle-leaved plant used in cooking is a herb.

clue.text: Fielder curt with member

parts.note: curt means brusque, short with someone
a member is a limb, such as a leg

explanation.surface: A rude cricket fielder with a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, short leg is a close fielding position on the leg side near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The player standing close in on the leg side is a type of fielder.

clue.text: Carry out what is required, as haulage firms do?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for fulfilling expectations or doing what was promised
taken literally, hauliers take merchandise to customers

explanation.surface: A wry nod to lorry companies, whose job is literally the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meet expectations, while its literal reading describes a carrier dropping off merchandise.

clue.text: Receive cut in advance with enthusiasm

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: advance as an adjective, as in advance warning, means early

indicators.note: cut says the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: to receive something is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone gets a share of the money ahead of time and is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' signals a docked final letter, and 'in' does double duty: it signals insertion and also belongs to the phrase 'in advance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly and with zest is doing it in an eager way.

clue.text: Get back about demand for payment

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a claim is a demand, for instance on an insurer

explanation.surface: Recovering money after chasing an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost or handed over is to take it back, a synonym.

clue.text: Section of coastline there, also heavenly

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travel writer calls part of the shoreline divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate and otherworldly, as if of the skies, is described with this synonym.

clue.text: International show certain to get publicity

parts.note: an expo is a large international exhibition
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A world fair is a guaranteed way to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Media attention or coverage given to someone is a synonym of publicity.

clue.text: Animal and large bird seen by river

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A wildlife scene: a creature and a big bird spotted at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madagascan primate with a long tail is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Men upset about the Spanish book on our former PM

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the rest
upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
el is the Spanish masculine word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men are angry about a Spanish book on a past leader of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals the anagram and 'about' the wrap; 'on' is only a link joining book and our.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Melbourne was Queen Victoria's first Prime Minister, so a former PM.

clue.text: Definite remedy

definitions.meaning: a medicine targeted at a particular disease

explanation.surface: A doctor declares the cure certain.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means precise; as an old noun it is a drug for one particular ailment.

clue.text: Hard leaving small community for capital

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for hard departs from the word

parts.note: a parish is a small local community around a church
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone finds it tough to quit village life for the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French seat of government is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Pasta meal in health centre, good dish wife ruled out

parts.note: a spa is a resort or centre for health treatments

indicators.note: ruled out says the letter for wife is excluded

parts.note: a bowl is a kind of dish

explanation.surface: A spa guest orders spaghetti, though the wife is barred from the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAG BOL is British slang for spaghetti bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of spaghetti in meat sauce is a popular pasta meal.

clue.text: Waste getting fancy wigs to be seen during ball

indicators.note: to be seen during places the rearranged letters within the other piece

parts.note: a pill is a small ball, and slang for a ball in games

indicators.note: fancy describes something elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extravagant headwear spotted at a dance looks like rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance, matching the wigs, but it is a small round object; 'fancy' signals the anagram and 'to be seen during' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps fed to hogs are a kind of food waste.

clue.text: What a gundog might do fetching bird?

definitions.meaning: a dog shakes its rear appendage when happy
a small long-tailed songbird of the genus Motacilla

explanation.surface: A retriever brings back game, perhaps contentedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog shaking its hindquarters does this, and it is also the name of a perky songbird.

clue.text: Ridiculous myths involving one place where metal is worked

indicators.note: involving says the jumbled letters take the other piece inside
ridiculous suggests nonsense, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Absurd legends about a forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculous' rearranges MYTHS to SMTHY, and 'involving' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop, where iron is hammered, is the kind of place described.

clue.text: Sword nicked by young woman

parts.note: nicked can mean slightly cut, as with a razor
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman wounded by a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved blade used by sailors and pirates is a kind of sword.

clue.text: School exercise

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to school is to teach or coach
as a verb, to exercise is to work out or drill

explanation.surface: PE lessons at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone and to work out in preparation are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: The French stable worker makes space

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A French stablehand clearing room in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to stretch out the lower limbs, as in a car or plane, is a kind of space.

clue.text: Rope also tight round head of stallion

indicators.note: round says the word goes around the extra letter
tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A cowboy pulls a rope taut round a wild horse's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the S from 'head of stallion' inside ALSO, and 'tight' rearranges the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed line for catching cattle is a kind of rope.

clue.text: Queen consort, during Belfast tour, reread novel

indicators.note: during puts the queen's name within the other words
reread suggests reading the letters again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Catherine Parr was the sixth wife and queen consort of Henry VIII

explanation.surface: A literature lover reads a book again on a trip around Northern Ireland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen consort' points to Henry VIII's last wife; 'during' signals the insertion and 'reread' the anagram of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes's 1984 book about a writer and a stuffed bird is a novel.

clue.text: Light in attic, and leaky!

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words that follow, across their breaks

explanation.surface: A homeowner finds a lamp in a loft that lets in rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick is a source of light, so the word names one example.

clue.text: Canine found next to railway could be mine

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog, a canine

explanation.surface: A dog by the tracks, which might belong to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, someone claiming the dog, but it is the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit with its buildings is a kind of mine.
